answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because ocean only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, ferrous is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any terrace approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
